analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy, 18 November 2026
key_insights: Nvidia reported after the US close with a decent earnings and revenue beat. It guided current-quarter sales to $130bn against a $125.3bn estimate and raised its forecast for next fiscal year revenue growth from 70% to 75%. Shares rose nearly 5% in extended trading after closing the regular session at their lowest since July 2025 (-0.44% on the day).
On the Nvidia call, the chairman said the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO.

Before the Nvidia release, the S&P 500 fell 1.03% to its lowest level since July. With Monday's 1.92% drop, this was the first pair of consecutive declines over 1% since March. Fears of an AI-related slowdown started the selloff and it broadened during the session.

Breadth was weak. 427 S&P 500 stocks declined and the equal-weighted index fell 1.45%. The Nasdaq fell 0.74%. The Philly semiconductor index rose 0.34% after falling 8.5% over the previous two sessions.

Overnight, Nasdaq futures are up 0.60% and S&P 500 futures up 0.24% after the Nvidia results. KOSPI (+1.79%) and Nikkei (+0.55%) are higher. Hang Seng (-1.00%) and ASX 200 (-0.69%) are lower. European futures are flat after big declines.

Treasuries rallied with the equity selloff even after St Louis Fed President Musalem said the economy will likely need several rate increases before spring 2027. The September 2027 rate, the peak on the curve, fell 4.2bps and markets now price 81bps of further Fed hikes at the peak. The 2yr yield fell 2.6bps to 4.80% and the 10yr fell 2.4bps to 5.11%. Both are down a further 1.5bps and 1.8bps overnight.

Oil rose on escalation fears. Iran's Mehr News Agency said the US attacked locations on Qeshm Island on Tuesday. Iran's negotiator Ghalibaf said any dam, port or power plant near a US or Israeli base is dual-use. Brent rose 0.76% to $93.14/bbl at the close.

US data was mixed. Retail sales rose 0.2% in October (vs +0.1% expected), industrial production fell 0.4% (vs +0.1% expected) and the NAHB housing index fell to 25 in November (vs 29 expected), the lowest since 2012. The Atlanta Fed GDPNow Q4 estimate moved from 3.5% to 3.4% annualised.

Europe sold off. The STOXX 600 fell 1.75%, its worst day since March, with the DAX down 2.08%, the CAC 40 down 1.62% and the FTSE 100 down 1.76%. Bund, OAT and BTP yields fell, with OATs (-8.0bps) outperforming as Marine Le Pen discussed potential pension reforms, which softened views of the RN candidate's fiscal proposals.

UK 10yr gilt yields rose 0.5bps after labour data. Unemployment fell to 4.6% in the 3 months to September (vs 4.7% expected), the lowest since April 2025, but payrolled employees fell 34k in October (vs +10k expected).
The German ZEW survey beat in November. Expectations rose to an 8-month high of 35.6 (vs 28.8 expected) and current conditions rose to -33.2 (vs -35.3 expected), the highest since April 2023.

Japan's October exports rose 20.5% YoY (vs 20.4% expected) to a record monthly level, led by semiconductor demand, for a 14th straight month of growth. Imports rose 21.6% YoY (vs 25.9% expected). A weak 20-year JGB auction saw the bid-to-cover ratio fall to 3.64 from 5.84, below the 12-month average of 3.92.

Today brings the Fed's October meeting minutes, speeches from Fed officials Daly, Barr, Williams and Kashkari, ECB President Lagarde and others, and BoE Governor Bailey. Data includes US housing starts, building permits and pending home sales, plus UK October CPI.

The author notes a run of technical outages: Apple's systems after an internal update, reported disruption on the NSA's internal network, Outlook, and the grounding of all US planes on Friday. He calls them apparent coincidences.
